title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 236 (Purchase of minority shareholding)

content.overview: Section 236 provides that in the event of an acquirer, or a person acting in concert with such acquirer, becoming registered holder of ninety per cent or more of the issued equity share capital of a company, or in the event of any person or group of persons becoming ninety per cent majority or holding ninety per cent of the issued equity share capital by virtue of an amalgamation, share exchange, conversion of securities or for any other reason, such acquirer or person or group shall notify the company of their intention to buy the remaining equity shares. The minority shareholders may also offer to sell. The price is determined by a registered valuer in accordance with prescribed rules. The amount is deposited in a separate bank account. The section is a takeover-completion device for the residual minority; it is not an oppression remedy under sections 241–242.
content.glance: Acquirer (with PACs) holds ≥90% of issued equity → must notify company of intention to buy remaining equity; minority may also require buy; price by registered valuer; deposit in separate account; distinct from s. 235 squeeze-out and from oppression.
content.study: Where an acquirer or persons acting in concert become the registered holders of ninety per cent or more of the issued equity share capital of a company, or where any person or group becomes a ninety per cent majority by amalgamation, share exchange, conversion or otherwise, such person shall notify the company of the intention to buy the remaining equity shares. Minority shareholders of the company may also offer to sell their shares. The price shall be determined by a registered valuer. Current-law framing: confirm 90%+ holding of issued equity (with PACs as applicable); notification of intention to buy remaining equity; minority may require purchase; registered-valuer price; deposit mechanism. Distinguish s. 235 (scheme-based squeeze-out after 9/10 approval) and ss. 241–242 (oppression and mismanagement).

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Acquirer (with persons acting in concert) holds 90% or more of issued equity share capital, or becomes 90% majority by amalgamation, share exchange, conversion or other reason.

sections.heading: Notification and Minority Right
sections.body: Acquirer must notify the company of intention to buy remaining equity; minority may also offer/require sale to the acquirer.

sections.heading: Price and Deposit
sections.body: Price determined by a registered valuer as prescribed; amount credited to a separate bank account.

sections.heading: Character
sections.body: Takeover-completion device for residual minority; not an oppression remedy.

examples.title: 90% acquirer notifies
examples.body: After a series of purchases, an acquirer with persons acting in concert holds 91% of the issued equity. Under s. 236 the acquirer must notify the company of the intention to buy the remaining equity shares at a registered-valuer price.

examples.title: Minority requires buy
examples.body: A residual minority shareholder, after the acquirer has crossed 90%, requires the acquirer to purchase the minority shares under s. 236 at the valuer-determined price.

hypotheticals.question: Is s. 236 the same as oppression relief under s. 241?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 236 is a statutory mechanism to complete a near-total equity holding by purchase of the residual minority at a registered-valuer price. Sections 241–242 address oppression and mismanagement with different standing, grounds and remedies.

distinctions.title: Purchase of minority (s. 236) vs squeeze-out of dissentients (s. 235)
distinctions.left: Acquirer already holds 90%+ of issued equity; notify and buy residual; minority may require buy
distinctions.right: Scheme/contract approved by 9/10 in value; notice to acquire dissentients

misconceptions.trap: Section 236 allows any majority to force out the minority at any price the majority chooses.
misconceptions.correction: Section 236 is triggered at the 90% issued-equity threshold. Price is determined by a registered valuer under the prescribed rules, not by unilateral majority fiat.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 236 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm 90%+ holding (with PACs). II. Notification and minority right to require buy. III. Registered-valuer price and deposit. IV. Distinguish s. 235 and oppression. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Holding facts; notification; valuation; precise relief.

content.migrationNote: Substantive enhancement. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

learningObjectives: State when minority shareholding may be purchased under s. 236.
Explain valuation and the distinction from s. 235 and oppression.
enhancement.definition: Section 236 requires an acquirer who (with persons acting in concert) holds ninety per cent or more of the issued equity share capital to notify the company of the intention to buy the remaining equity shares at a registered-valuer price; the minority may also require the purchase.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Once equity ownership is concentrated at or above ninety per cent, residual minority interests can be completed by a statutory purchase at an independent valuation.
essentialIngredients: 90%+ of issued equity (acquirer with PACs or by amalgamation/exchange/conversion)
Notification of intention to buy remaining equity
Price by registered valuer; deposit in separate account
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 236 is the residual-minority purchase rule after concentration of equity ownership.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm threshold; notify; value; complete purchase.

verification.note: Section-text level; valuation rules are prescribed separately; case-law verification separate; no new citations invented.

distinctions: Purchase of minority (s. 236) vs squeeze-out of dissentients (s. 235)
